dedupe_keys.name: replication package for what can country panels tell us about broadband price responsiveness evidence from the european union and the eastern partnership 2010 2024

description: Samir Orujov and colleagues publish a broadband-price responsiveness replication package. Zenodo archives public code, data and results under MIT and links a repository. The description identifies a 2010–2024 panel for 27 EU and six Eastern Partnership countries using ITU price baskets, World Bank indicators and harmonised night-time lights, plus a panel of 175 EU NUTS-2 regions from Eurostat. These inputs can inform broadband-adoption or network-demand scenarios, with the study code providing sensitivity context. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this price panel. Coverage is selected European countries and regions, not household subscription records or a map of physical fibre links. A limitation is that country-level associations cannot establish a subscriber-level price response or a causal effect without the paper’s assumptions. The repository archive was not downloaded, the pipeline was not run and numerical elasticities were not independently checked.
